review_findings.basis: The migration defines the index IF NOT EXISTS. The readiness matcher checks containment of table, name, and the two leading fields. It also accepts an incompatible UNIQUE suffix. Same-episode rows are allowed to share a timestamp. A pre-existing unique index can pass on empty or non-colliding data, then block colliding backfill or access writes.

review_findings.basis: The local adapter retries transient errors and applies a separate timeout retry budget. The comment says only transaction conflicts are retried. The guarded exact assignments and cursor in one commit make replay idempotent without that assumption.

contracts_rechecked.migration_and_ownership: 057 DDL is additive. Signed nonzero or timestamp-only legacy rows are copied in bound 128-key pages, checking exact pre-existing values and committing the owner-guarded cursor in the same transaction. Entire eligible coverage is reconciled before application marking. Failed/applied terminal updates compare applying status and owner. 057 is in the tenant digest; the runbook fences old binaries operationally through readiness.
contracts_rechecked.write_and_retry: The predecessor app SQL already used atomic UPDATE RETURN NONE; the isolation changes physical write targets, rather than removing any predecessor full-record application retry. First access projects persisted source_episode only. Existing rows write only the side table. Both signed saturation branches guard addition, zero boost still stamps, one timestamp is bound across retries, and absent fact with no side row is a no-op. This does not establish increment exactly-once under ambiguous commit acknowledgement.
contracts_rechecked.read_and_usage: Missing rows become zero/empty. Database and invalid row-shape, key, count or timestamp errors propagate through exact bounded reads into all seven pre-fusion channels and decay preflight. Decay performs its heat reads before mutation; archival separates active-fact and recent-access decisions. Revision-bounded historical recall bypasses mutable heat.
contracts_rechecked.await_and_failure: Warm and cold tracking await four-wide waves with repeated IDs ordered. Explain awaits its boost. Successful issued writes are awaited before return; failed attempts are logged and sibling/later writes settle, potentially with successful recall. A settled marker describes completion of attempts, not proof every write committed. Controlled cancellation proves ownership of application futures, not rollback of arbitrary in-flight engine work.
